text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's rural communities, struggling to survive under biting economic reforms, are set to benefit from a Z$1.1 billion two-year World Bank rural infrastructure development programme set to start this year, the bank's resident representative in Zimbabwe David Cook told the Financial Gazette.
- The state-owned Commercial Bank of Zimbabwe on Wednesday launched what is set to become the single largest public share offering by a financial institution, expected to raise Z$512 million.

- The Business Herald says Zimbabwe president Robert Mugabe intervened during his visit to Malaysia last week to resolve a stalemate which had apparently developed between the Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority and YTL Corp of Malaysia over negotiations to privatise the southern African country's Hwange Thermal Power Station.
- A local cable manufacturing company, BICCCAFCA has lost a Z$0.5 billion tender to supply cables to the Posts and Telecommunications Corp to a foreign firm.

- Land and Agriculture Minister Kumbirai Kangai and farming leaders on Wednesday warned an annual congress of the Commercial Farmers Union that drought could hit the country during the next agricultural season due to El Nino and said farmers should brace themselves accordingly.
- The Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority is losing at least Z$60,000 worth of copper conductors in Harare every month to thieves.
